content: If you stay in the center and embrace death with your whole heart, you will endure forever.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing), Book of the Way
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

Across his life and work, Lao Tzu saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: What quiet yearning in your heart is asking for your attention and honest devotion?
